title: Suntrack Hub 2: practical semi-D factories on a truck route.
location: Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, Sepang, Selangor
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #421 | SUNTRACK HUB 2, SALAK TINGGI
excerpt: 62 individual-title semi-D factories on a main road off the ELITE highway, near KLIA. Sean likes the access, the security-only maintenance fee and the practical design, but notes the competition and the utilities next door.
takeaways: Leasehold semi-D factories of about 7,600 to 8,400 sq ft built-up, priced around RM540 psf, or about RM4.1 to RM4.5 million.
Owners pay about RM500 a month for security only; roads and drains stay with the local authority.
Nearby industrial lots rent for about RM2 psf, roughly RM17,000 to RM18,000 a month for the larger type.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Suntrack Hub 2 puts 62 leasehold semi-detached factories with individual titles on 26.34 acres, in two phases. Owners sign a deed of mutual covenant and pay about RM500 a month purely for the guardhouse, CCTV at junctions and patrols, while the roads, drains and sewerage remain with the local authority, as at the developer's first hub in Bangi.

Type A sits on 72 by 170 ft lots with about 8,400 sq ft built-up, and Type B has about 7,600 sq ft. Each has a warehouse floor about 6 m high with a 9 m clear span at the back, roller shutters, a ramp, a canopy extended to the rear boundary, and half a floor of office space, a prayer room and pantry upstairs. The site is cut from high ground to about 1 m above the latest flood level, with floors rated for heavy loads.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site fronts Jalan Labohan Dagang, the road trucks use between the North-South and ELITE highways to bypass KL, lined with petrol stations, and is close to KLIA. Shop offices, eateries and licensed workers' quarters stand in front, KIP Mall is 5 to 10 minutes away, and a sewage treatment plant, a water pump house, a retention pond and a pylon reserve border the site.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: At about RM540 psf, a Type A unit costs about RM4.5 million and a Type B about RM4.1 million. Industrial space around the area rents for about RM2 psf, roughly RM17,000 to RM18,000 a month for a Type A used as back of house, more for units with main-road frontage.

standout.title: Paying only for security
standout.body: Instead of a strata-style arrangement where owners eventually pay to repair roads and drains, buyers form a residents' body that collects about RM500 a month for the guardhouse and CCTV alone. Infrastructure maintenance stays with the local authority, a model the developer proved at its first hub in Bangi.

pros: The location: on the main road that serves as the trucks' shortcut between the North-South and ELITE highways, where industrial lots cluster, with KLIA next door as a bonus.

The immediate setting: a wide, well-built road with petrol stations, units connected to the road rather than tucked away, and existing workers' quarters, eateries and services beside the site, with KIP Mall a short drive away.

The practicality: security-only fees, a site cut to solid ground above flood level, strong floors, and simple, user-focused units with high ceilings, roller shutters, ramps, bathrooms, extended canopies, plenty of street parking and a plain facade ready for signage.
cons: Competition: many industrial parks of different sizes and prices line the same corridor, so investors should compare several before buying.
Scale: with only 62 units, the park lacks the name of a large industrial address, which may matter to big corporate or logistics users.
Utilities around the site: a retention pond, sewage treatment plant and pylon reserve, though he sees little real harm for an industrial owner and might even prefer the extra setback.

closing: A practical, well-connected factory for owner-operators and investors who check flood levels, floor loading and power needs against their business.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this January 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the site, the model and a built unit while earthworks were under way; prices are the team's and the rental estimate is Sean's.
